_comment: An EXAMPLE store pack — the shape the cloud sends this box (EDGE_PACK_FILE).
Every top-level section is optional, and leaving one out is meaningful:
the box then tells the screens it has NOT BEEN TOLD that section, which is
different from telling them the section is empty. The manager's day close
refuses the first and proceeds on the second.
Contains no real store data, no prices anybody trades on and no secrets.
deliveries/drivers/routingPolicy: the box PLANS the routes itself from these,
so vans still go out when the internet is down. `route` overrides the planner
when a dispatcher writes one by hand, and the driver's screen says which it is.
Distances are straight-line: there is no map here, so the plan is a draft.
purchaseOrders/receipts/supplierInvoices/buyingPolicy: the buyer's screen.
Leave buyingPolicy out and the box serves the buyer's screen nothing at all,
because a screen inventing its own match tolerances would be deciding how big
a price difference is worth nobody's attention. The buyer must NOT appear in
approvers: nobody signs off their own capture (roadmap section 28).
categories/productMaster/priceEntries/pricingPolicy: the product and price screen.
Leave pricingPolicy out and the box serves that screen nothing, because a screen
inventing its own margin floor would be deciding how much of the shop's profit is
worth nobody's attention. The person who sets prices must NOT be in approvers.
A product with no unitCostMinor has NO entry in the cost map served to that screen
- not a zero. Zero cost reports a 100% margin, which is a lie that reads as good news.
shelfLocations/shelfAssignments/shelfPolicy: where things sit (M04-FR-02).
This is what puts the picker's list in the order they walk the shop, and every
field is a NUMBER because 'A10' sorts before 'A9' as text and the picker then
walks the aisle twice without ever knowing why. zoneOrder is YOUR cold-chain
decision - leave it out and the walk is ordered by position only, and every
screen says so rather than implying a cold chain nobody asked for.
planogram/shelfCounts/backstock/assortment/spaceAreas/displayContracts: merchandising.
Leave merchandisingPolicy out and the box serves that screen nothing, because a
screen inventing its own refill level would be deciding when a shelf is empty
enough to be worth walking to. A facing with NO count in shelfCounts is reported
as 'never counted' - it is NOT treated as empty, which would raise the loudest
alarm the system has for every product in the shop on day one.
reportingRecords/roles/roleAssignments/reportingPolicy: the reporting screen (D13).
reportingRecords is what this shop ACTUALLY records today, and the gaps are the
point: a report whose fact is not in this list REFUSES BY NAME rather than running
and coming back as zero, because a zero is read as 'nothing happened' and an empty
report is read as 'nothing to worry about'. Leave reportingPolicy out and the box
serves that screen nothing, because a screen inventing its own staleness thresholds
would be deciding, on its own authority, how old a number may be before somebody
should stop making decisions on it. roles/roleAssignments are the shop's OWN access
control, so the same default-deny check that guards an action guards its export.
returnHistory/serviceCases/satisfaction/slaPolicy/servicePolicy: the service desk.
Leave servicePolicy out and the box serves that screen nothing, because a screen
inventing its own return window would be deciding how long this shop takes goods
back for, and inventing its own refund threshold would be deciding how much money
may leave without a second signature. returnHistory is the returns the CLOUD knows
about - another branch's, or ones taken before this box was installed. It is MERGED
with the box's own return log, never replaced by it: the cloud alone leaves the
at-most-once guard blind exactly when the line is down, which is when a shop is
least supervised. THE FIVE NUMBERS IN servicePolicy ARE YOURS TO SET before go-live
- the ones here are starting figures, not a recommendation.
